question: What is the meaning of book value in relation to value information?
description: The book value in relation to value information refers to the recorded cost of an asset as shown on a company's balance sheet. It represents the net asset value of a company, calculated as total assets minus total liabilities. In the context of sustainable construction and material passports, book value may not directly apply, as material passports focus on the characteristics and potential future value of materials rather than their historical cost. However, understanding book value can still be relevant when assessing the financial aspects of projects involving sustainable materials and technologies.

“Nutrient Certificates, or Materials Passports as they are often 
referred to, are sets of data describing defined characteristics of 
materials in products that give them value for present use as well as 
recovery and reuse. The passports are a marketplace mechanism to 
encourage product designs, material recovery systems, and chain of 
possession partnerships that improve the quality, value, and security 
of supply for materials so they can be reused in continuous loops or 
closed loops or beneficially returned to biological systems. This is 
done by adding a new value dimension to materials quality. This new 
dimension is based on the suitability of materials for healthy present 
use as well as recovery and reuse as resources in other products and 
processes.” (The work of Hansen et al. (2012) is (yearly) revisited
